How settlement really works on Erasmus Mundus: You study in 2–3 countries, but your post-study right to stay is usually tied to the country where you finish and where your diploma is issued — not every country you visited. The smart move is to choose your final semester in the country you most want to settle in, and confirm that with the consortium before you accept a mobility track.

Which country gives the longest runway?

For a master's graduate. Longer is not automatically better — language, lab jobs and whether the permit lets you actually work matter just as much.

What to do now — in deadline order

1
Book IELTS Academic now — don't wait.

IMIM and Europubhealth+ close 4–8 January and neither exempts Nigeria on a medium-of-instruction letter. You need a test result in hand, not a booking. Target: IELTS 6.5, no section below 6.0.

2
Get the MOI letter anyway — it unlocks LIVE.

Ask the university for a certificate confirming the BSc was taught in English. LIVE_Innov accepts that instead of IELTS/TOEFL if it covers at least 6 months of successful study in English.

3
Confirm two numbers: exact CGPA + graduation year.

MemBioMed needs CGPA ≥ 3.25 / 5.0 (65%) and a degree from 2023 or later. Below 3.25 or earlier than 2023, drop it and focus energy elsewhere.

4
Prepare the shared pack once.

Degree + transcript (with official English translation if needed), passport, CV, 2 reference letters, motivation letter tailored per course. Almost every consortium asks for the same core set.

5
Choose your settlement country before you choose your track.

On Europubhealth+ and IMIM you pick pathways. Put Ireland (24 months, English-speaking) or Germany / Netherlands (large lab & pharma markets) last if settlement is the priority.

University of Groningen, Netherlands — coordinator of IMIM and one of the strongest settlement bases: 12-month Orientation Year, then a reduced salary threshold for the Highly Skilled Migrant permit.

The scholarship, plainly

€1,400 / month for up to 24 months for scholarship holders, paid by the consortium. No tuition or participation fees, and insurance is covered.

That €1,400 has to cover travel, visa, installation and living costs — there is no separate travel grant. Budget for the first month in each new country: deposits and registration often land before the next instalment.

Not everyone selected gets a scholarship. IDOHNext, for example, awards only a few per intake to top-ranked students among those selected. Always check whether an offer is scholarship or self-funded before accepting.

This is a starting shortlist, not immigration advice. Visa and residence rules change — verify deadlines on the consortium site and settlement rules on the official immigration site of the country you plan to finish in.

Sources for course rules: consortium sites linked in each course detail. Settlement summaries checked Nov 2026 against official and government guidance, including the Netherlands Business.gov.nl orientation-year page. Deadlines shown are scholarship deadlines for Sep 2027 entry.
